chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Haysam al-Ajali (may God be pleased with him) narrated that Abul-Abbas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qattan narrated that Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib narrated that Tamim ibn Buhlool narrated that Abu Muawiyah, from Suleiman ibn Mihran, from Ja'far ibn Muhammad, from his father, from his grandfather, from his father Al-Hussein ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (peace be upon them) said: I heard God's Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) say:

Indeed, the nation of Moses divided after him into seventy-one sects, one of them saved and seventy in Hell. The nation of Jesus (peace be upon him) divided after him into seventy-two sects, one of them saved and seventy-one in Hell. And indeed, my nation will divide after me into seventy-three sects, one of them saved and seventy-two in Hell.
ai.seo_question: How many sects will the Muslim Ummah divide into according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, this hadith establishes the 'Firqat al-Najiya' (Saved Sect) as the followers of the Ahl al-Bayt, grounding their theological authority in the Prophet’s prediction of seventy-three divisions. It draws a direct parallel to the fracturing of the Israelites and Christians, positioning the Shi'a as the continuation of the true monotheistic tradition amidst widespread deviation. This narrative serves as a foundational criterion for distinguishing orthodoxy from heresy in Shia jurisprudence and theology.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 24-11 Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Haysam al-Ajali - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Abul-Ab’bas Ahmad ibn Yahya ibn Zakariya al-Qat’tan quoted Bakr ibn Abdullah ibn Habib, on the authority of Tamim ibn Buhlool, on the authority of Abu Muawiyah, on the authority of Suleiman ibn Mihran, on the authority of Ja’far ibn Muhammad as-Sadiq (as), on the authority of his father (ra), on the authority of his grandfather (MGB), on the authority of his father Al-Hussein ibn Ali ibn Abi Talib (as) that he had heard God’s Prophet (sw) say, “

Indeed the nation of Moses (as) divided up into seventy-one sects after him. One sect shall be saved and the other seventy sects will go to Hell. The nation of Jesus (as) divided up into seventy-two sects after him. One sect shall be saved and the other seventy-one sects will go to Hell. My nation will be divided up into seventy-three sects after me. One sect will be saved and the other seventy-two sects will go to Hell.”
